itemtext.why: No item text for this PR, per #3421.

notes: openESM's copy has 47 rows (sittings) with no sitting_id and every survey item empty, while the original deposit (cleanData.rds) has survey answers for all 47: each is a sitting with no Digit-Symbol row there. Shipped as openESM's copy is, so those 47 sittings (1.5%) are missing. Every shipped value in the other 3,062 sittings matches the original.
For the openESM report (#1698): 0003_hawks loses the survey answers of 47 sittings that have no Digit-Symbol row in cleanData.rds; and study_time is the original's fraction of a day multiplied by 24.
Instruments are named from the openESM codebook 0003_hawks_codebook.pdf (the paper's supplement, S1). It cites no source for the attentional items, so none is named here.

The contextual items (going_on, concentrating, noisy) are not shipped: the codebook lists them under 'Contextual Items' with no source or score, the supplement's models enter each as a separate predictor, and they describe different things (surroundings, noise, one's own concentration).

flags.what: no time stamps or counter: `wave` = (day - day_min) * beeps_per_day + (beep - beep_min) + 1. Check beeps_per_day against the sampling scheme ('3x/day fixed time windows'); no `date`.
flags.resolution: wave = day * 4 + beep (day 0-9). The scheme is 3 sittings a day, but beep 4 occurs twice (a fourth sitting, CT54 day 1 and PT55 day 8), so beeps_per_day is 4 and waves have gaps. sitting_id and study_time order agree with day/beep everywhere. No `date`: study_time is clock time without a calendar date.

flags.what: 2 proposed table(s) hold a single item (hawks_2023_social_functioning_s, hawks_2023_sleepiness). Decide for each whether it belongs with a neighbouring table of the same questionnaire, stands alone, or is not shipped.
flags.resolution: socialfunc_interactions and alert_sleepiness are not shipped: single items, under the 3-item floor (datastandard.md).

flags.what: Tables are a first guess from file order, response scale, source, prompts asked at, and column-name prefixes. Read the codebook and split or merge so each table is one instrument or subscale (datastandard.md, 'One file per scale'); rename each `<author>_<year>_<construct>`, and set `script` to the record's name.
flags.resolution: Four tables from the openESM codebook 0003_hawks_codebook.pdf (the paper's supplement, S1): PANAS short form split into its positive- and negative-affect subscales (the codebook's own grouping), the Anxiety & Depression Scale, and the attentional items. The six Daily Inventory of Stressful Events items are not shipped, as for 0075_ballou: 1 = not endorsed is mixed with 2-5 stress ratings and each item is a different event. covid_stress is the DISE's sixth prompt, coded the same way. The contextual items are not shipped (see notes).

flags.what: `candidates` holds columns that may or may not be items (binary checkboxes, counts, rating scales whose coding gives no anchors -- sleep_duration, social_functioning_composite, ds_median_r_tc, test_position, crt_median_r_tc, gcpt_dprime, mot_percent_correct). Move any that are responses into a table; the rest go to `not_shipped` with a reason. sleep_duration, social_functioning_composite, ds_median_r_tc, test_position, crt_median_r_tc, gcpt_dprime, mot_percent_correct
flags.resolution: All seven to not_shipped: four cognitive-task summaries (median RT, d-prime, proportion correct), a social-functioning composite, a derived sleep duration, and test position.
